notes.text: A handwritten working sheet. The lower-left pencil number is 37 and is retained as an archive-number comment. No author’s page number, date or page title is visible. Section 1.3 and display labels (17), (22), (23), (24), (25) are present.

The source opening says ‘Mais si cette condition n’est pas satisfaite’ and ‘on reste en plan’, then writes C as the disjoint unions of the two Pi and omega objects and lists the four epsilon-labelled elements. These are reported as source statements.

The source singles out epsilon1+ < epsilon2- and epsilon2+ < epsilon1-. The diagram draws four black points and exactly those two upward crossing arrows. The lower-left-to-upper-right shaft is continuous at the crossing; the other shaft has a central gap. The cancelled lower label reads epsilon2+.

Section 1.3 cancels an initial family phrase, then writes (23), with Sigma carrying lower alpha and upper epsilon and the enclosing family indexed by epsilon in omega_alpha. The prose changes famille to an interlinear ens. parenthesis. The subsequent source condition (24) quantifies alpha,beta in A and alpha neq beta before its phrase non panachées.

The first slanted note begins c’est un élément de. The three angular capitals and older crossing are retained with the stated glyph/state uncertainties. Its written parenthesis segment is )(X)); no expected interpretation of the expression was used to move parentheses.

The second slanted note writes Card A=n and names an underlined décomposition n-aire non panachée de X. The n reading comes from the rounded shoulder and its repeated shape before -aire. Both separately drawn underline stretches are represented.

The raised underlined heading reads Déf without a terminal point. The source cancels alors and uses non panachée in the definition, with a singular/plural uncertainty at that occurrence. Its parenthesis gives analogous terminology with strictement underlined.

The source writes C as a coproduct indexed by alpha in A in (25). The addition to its right begins ‘avec l’involution ss pt fixe sigma’, contains ‘qui, sur chaque omega_alpha, induit une ... transposition’, and includes one heavily cancelled unreadable word. The final main-line text ends on the isolated a at the bottom.

H’s explicit notes were read: it calls the diagram elements points and acknowledges a cancelled item below epsilon1+; it calls both marginal notes oblique notes in the left margin; and it identifies the sigma passage as an interlinear addition to the right of (25), ending the page on a. H’s further reference to a title on page 31 was not checked against another page. Its sigma placement note is respected, so no whole-group insertion omission is charged there.

Mathematical notation served only as local reading context: the visible 1/2 forms in the diagram were compared for the cancelled suffix, the epsilon body has two vertical turns, and omega has two rounded shallow bowls. No theorem was proved, no computation was certified, and no mathematical result was substituted for written ink.
